text.p: PRESS DIGEST - Romania - Aug 8
Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The Darmanesti, Petrotel and Vega oil refineries are to be shut down and its 8,000 employees laid off.

- The transport ministry will offer concessions for four highways -- Bucharest-Pitesti, 96 km, Bucharest-Constanta, 201 km, Bucharest-Giurgiu, 44 km and the southern part of the highway around Bucharest, 58 km.
- The Italian consortium Frederici Astaldi Todini is to sign in September a contract to start works on the Bucharest-Pitesti highway.
- West Merchant Bank will grant a $300 million credit to help upgrade Romania's road and rail infrastructure.
ADEVARUL ECONOMIC
- The newspaper publishes a report on the rise of arrears and inventories in Romania's economy.
ADEVARUL
- The newspaper presents excerpts from Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea's news conference saying that structural reform in Romania can no longer be delayed.
- Romania must have a considerable rise in foreign investment next year, says Poul Thomsen, chief negotiator of the International Monetary Fund in an interview.
- The health ministry is to cut another 5,000 jobs starting September.

- Romania's Romtelecom telephone authority to be privatised and starting September 1 the former regie autonomme will become Romania's first state-owned joint-stock company, Communications Minister Sorin Pantis said.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- The newspaper publishes a full-page report on the state of tourism in Romania.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The newspaper publishes the list of 17 state-run companies which are to be shut down as they had accumulated losses and debts of over two trillion lei.
- Alexandru Nicolae, head of the Senate's Defence Commission, said people in Prahova county prepare big protests against the creation of a structure to replace the National oil Company.
General:
ADEVARUL
- The newspaper publishes opinions by party leaders on the decision to place bilingual plaques for towns and villages.

- Police chief Pavel Abraham said some countries had confirmed that only 10-15 Romanian children of 1,200-1,500 adopted by foreigners had actually entered those countries, although they had left Romania.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
